reading.body:
H.R. 8241, the Power for the People Act of 2026, is a one-party energy and data center bill with 29 Democratic sponsors and no lobbying filings naming it.

Every sponsor and cosponsor recorded here is a Democrat, led by Paul Tonko. The bill's own text is tagged to energy and data centers, which places it in the same policy space as the state and local rules governing where AI compute may be built and who pays for its power. The cosponsor list is heavily drawn from Maryland, Illinois, and California members, though the data does not explain why those states are overrepresented.

The absence of lobbying filings is the notable fact. Zero filings for 2025 or later name this bill, which means the lobbying record cannot show who is trying to influence it or which direction they want it to go. A filing that names a bill shows only that the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken, and here there are none to read at all.

What this does not cover: the bill's text, its committee status, any recorded votes, or its prospects. The latest status date is 2026-04-09, and the data stops there. Nothing here establishes that this bill will move, or that it will affect data center siting or power costs if it does.

summary: H.R. 8241, Power for the People Act of 2026. Latest status date 2026-04-09. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. 0 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
